Lares helps you spend less time on distracting apps and websites. A trusted person – your guardian – holds the code that protects your rules. First a short tour, then your guardian sets everything up.
You decide which apps and websites Lares restricts. Each one is a rule.
Add apps from the list or type in a website – also just a part of it, e.g. youtube.com/shorts.
Templates add popular apps together with their websites and alternative apps in one go.
Groups let several apps and websites share one limit, e.g. all social media together.
Every rule or group gets one of these modes:
A number of minutes per day. A countdown shows the last minutes, then it’s blocked until the daily reset.
Different rules for different times and days – see the next page.
A schedule is a weekly time table. On each day you add windows that are blocked, have a timer or are free. For the time outside the windows you choose what applies.
Example week: on weekdays blocked during school hours and a short timer in the evening, free on Saturday afternoon, a timer on Sunday.
Schedules are created in the settings and can be picked for any rule or group. Windows can be moved and resized like calendar entries.
Your guardian sets up a password or an authenticator app. It stays with them – that’s what makes the rules stick.
Changing rules needs the code – by default every change, so nothing is added by mistake.
With the code, Lares is unlocked for 10 minutes, and the guardian can start a pause.
Optional protections prevent uninstalling and notify your guardian about tampering.
Lares is ready. On the main screen, add apps and websites with “Add”; schedules are created in the settings. Your guardian can change the rules with the code at any time.
There’s also a browser extension: Lares Browser Edition blocks websites in your browser on a computer.
It’s a separate project, set up on its own, and may not have every feature of the newest app version yet.

Lares works entirely on this phone.

• No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking, no crash reporting.
• No data is sold. Nothing is shared with third parties – except the notification services you set up yourself (see below).
• Your rules, usage times, settings and a log of protection events (e.g. “clock changed”) are stored only on this phone. They are excluded from Android backups and device transfers.
• The guardian code is stored only as a protected hash (password) or encrypted with a key that never leaves this phone (authenticator app) – an authenticator code additionally encrypted with the recovery code, for moving it to a new phone. The recovery code is stored only as a protected hash.
• Lares turns off Android autofill, so password managers never offer to save the guardian code.
• If you turn on the Accessibility service or usage access, Lares uses it only to detect which app is open – and, while website blocking is on, the address in the address bar of supported browsers and, while “Guard system settings” is on, whether a system settings page or uninstall dialog is about Lares (nothing else of the screen). This is processed on the phone in the moment and neither stored nor sent.
• The optional device administrator role is only used to prevent uninstalling Lares.
• Lares connects to the internet only to send guardian notifications – and only to the services set up in the settings (Telegram, ntfy, email, Matrix or a webhook). Nothing is sent unless such a channel is set up. A message contains only the notification text (e.g. “protection was disabled”), its time and the phone model; the chosen service’s own privacy policy applies. Tokens and passwords are stored encrypted on the phone.
• Some links open in your browser, which loads them: Lares’ neutral page shown when a website is blocked (hosted on GitHub Pages; GitHub’s privacy policy applies), manufacturer tips, the browser extension’s project page (GitHub) and library pages.
• Exported rule files contain rules, groups and schedules – no tokens or usage data. If switched on, they also contain the authenticator code, encrypted with the recovery code (useless without it); never the password.
